title: Altered mechanical and vascular responses of the Achilles tendon to acute loading in Kendo athletes.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to elucidate acute, bilateral Achilles tendon (AT) responses to high-intensity single-leg hopping in Kendo athletes and healthy controls.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty Kendo athletes and 20 sedentary controls performed a single-leg hopping task. Ultrasound imaging assessed AT anteroposterior diameter (APD), shear wave velocity (SWV), and intratendinous vessel count before (PRE), immediately after (POST), and 5-min post-exercise (POST5).
RESULTS: Following exercise, Kendo athletes exhibited a significant main effect of time for both APD (P = 0.012) and SWV (P = 0.012), regardless of side. No significant acute changes in APD or SWV were observed in the control group. For intratendinous vascularity, a significant side-by-time interaction was observed in Kendo athletes (P = 0.026): the right leg showed no significant change, whereas the left leg exhibited a progressive increase from PRE to POST (P < 0.001) and further increased at POST5 (P = 0.002). In the control group, vessel count significantly increased at POST (P = 0.023) but rapidly returned to baseline. In the three-way analyses, no significant Group × Side × Time interaction was observed for any imaging outcome.
CONCLUSION: Within Kendo athletes, morphological and mechanical responses occurred bilaterally, whereas the temporal vascular response differed between the left and right Achilles tendons. However, this side-specific vascular pattern was not shown to differ significantly from that observed in sedentary controls.

title: Hydrogels as drug carriers for cartilage repair in osteoarthritis: Applications and challenges.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage degradation, subchondral bone remodelling, synovial inflammation, osteophyte formation, and loss of joint function, resulting in significant pain, disability, and socioeconomic burden worldwide. Despite advances in clinical management, current therapeutic strategies, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, corticosteroids, hyaluronic acid injections, and surgical interventions, primarily provide symptomatic relief and have limited ability to prevent disease progression or regenerate damaged cartilage. In recent years, hydrogel-based drug delivery systems have emerged as promising therapeutic platforms owing to their excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, injectability, high water content, and structural similarity to the native extracellular matrix. These properties enable hydrogels to serve as effective carriers for a wide range of therapeutic agents, including anti-inflammatory drugs, growth factors, nucleic acids, nanoparticles, exosomes, and stem cells, while providing sustained and localized drug release within the osteoarthritic joint. This review comprehensively discusses the pathophysiology of OA and highlights the major molecular signaling pathways involved in disease progression, including NF-κB, MAPK, Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, TGF-β, and JAK/STAT pathways. Furthermore, recent advances in natural, synthetic, hybrid, and stimuli-responsive hydrogels are critically examined, with particular emphasis on their applications in cartilage repair and targeted drug delivery. Emerging approaches involving nanotechnology-enabled hydrogels, gene delivery systems, stem cell-loaded constructs, and immunomodulatory biomaterials are also evaluated for their therapeutic potential and translational prospects. This review provides an integrated and up-to-date perspective on hydrogel-based strategies for cartilage regeneration and disease modification, highlighting their potential as next-generation therapeutic platforms for the long-term management of osteoarthritis.

title: Understanding the Complexity of Athlete Sleep: A Systems Approach to Modelling the Athlete Sleep Environment.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Athlete sleep can be disrupted by sport- and non-sport-related factors. However, the interactions of these sleep-related factors are not well understood. Systems science approaches, such as causal loop diagramming (CLD), provide an opportunity to map these interactions. This project aimed to (1) develop a CLD of the athlete sleep system describing the interacting variables, (2) identify feedback loops and potential leverage points to optimise athlete sleep, and (3) demonstrate the applicability of a CLD to guide the development of a sleep monitoring framework.
METHODS: A systems-based model of athlete sleep was developed using CLD, informed by existing literature and refined through a consensus process involving ten subject matter experts (nine from Australia, one from the USA). The model was then interrogated using network analysis to identify key variables based on their position and connectivity within the system. These findings informed the development of a generic sleep monitoring framework.
RESULTS: The CLD comprised 48 variables and 120 relationships across four domains: travel demands, behavioural and lifestyle factors, athlete condition and readiness, and resourcing and scheduling constraints. Overall, 12 key variables were identified, with hours of travel, number of time zones crossed, dose of caffeine, and amount of resources or expenditure available being the most connected upstream variables. Level of pre-sleep arousal, sleep opportunity, travel fatigue, and level of performance received the greatest number of incoming relationships, representing points at which multiple pathways converge. Physical condition, level of performance, quality of diet, and importance of competition most frequently linked different quadrants of the system. These variables informed a three-tier monitoring framework capturing upstream determinants and downstream consequences of sleep.
CONCLUSIONS: According to the CLD, sleep health in athletes extends beyond an individual behaviour issue and is influenced by the structure and functioning of sport systems. Interactions among travel demands, physical readiness, behavioural and lifestyle factors, and organisational constraints sustain athlete sleep health over time. Consequently, meaningful improvements in sleep health are likely to arise from both system-level interventions and individual behaviour change strategies.

title: Treatment of clavicle fractures in adolescents.
abstract: Clavicle fractures constitute 10% to 15% of all fractures in adolescents. Historically, adolescent clavicle fractures have been treated non-operatively. Although recent data in the adult population has led to an increased rate of operative fixation in the adolescent population, a vast majority of these fractures in adolescents can be managed conservatively. This manuscript provides an overview of the current standard of care for clavicular fractures in adolescents in the context of sports medicine practices. To achieve this, a nonsystematic search of computerized databases of peer-reviewed articles was conducted, and a critical appraisal of existing literature was subsequently performed. Middle third clavicle fractures are by far the most common type and a vast majority of these fractures can be treated non-operatively with a sling given the robust healing and remodeling seen in adolescents. Lateral third fractures are far less common but may pose a risk for nonunion according to adult literature. Medial third fractures are the least common type and while they are typically non-displaced, patients with posteriorly displaced medial third fractures must have concomitant intrathoracic injury ruled out. Additionally, timing of the injury relative to competitive season could play a role in decision making as surgical fixation of clavicle fractures has been shown to yield faster return to play times.

title: Excessive COX-Prostaglandin Signaling Promotes Cellular Senescence and Impaired Skeletal Muscle Recovery in Aging.
abstract: The ability to recover skeletal muscle after periods of disuse declines with age leading to persistent deficits in strength and function that extend beyond muscle mass loss. Here, we investigated whether age-related alterations in lipid remodeling contribute to impairment in skeletal muscle recovery following disuse. Lipidomic and oxylipin profiling revealed that aged mouse muscle is characterized by sustained phosphatidylcholine and omega-6-dependent COX-prostaglandin signaling during early recovery from disuse atrophy. This persistent lipid mediator response was associated with increased senescence burden, fibrosis, and impaired functional recovery. Pharmacological suppression of COX signaling during reloading in aged mice reduced senescence markers, limited fibrosis, and improved muscle function independent of improved muscle size. Mechanistically, senescent induced macrophages produced COX-2-dependent PGE2 and impaired myotube size and fusion through paracrine signaling. Activation of EP2 signaling was sufficient to induce a senescent macrophage phenotype. Importantly, a similar age-associated dysregulation of oxylipin content was observed in older adults after limb immobilization, supporting the translational relevance of these findings. Together, our results identify sustained COX-prostaglandin signaling as a key feature of impaired skeletal muscle recovery with aging and suggest that targeted modulation of this pathway may improve muscle recovery in older individuals. title: Effects of Resveratrol Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) is a common consequence of high-intensity or unfamiliar physical activity and can lead to muscle soreness, inflammation, oxidative stress, and temporary loss of muscle function. Although various interventions have been explored to alleviate EIMD, resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic compound found in grapes, berries, and other plants, has attracted attention due to its potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This review aims to explore the effects of RES on EIMD in terms of its impact on muscle recovery, inflammation, and oxidative stress markers. This review synthesizes the results of preclinical and clinical studies and highlights the timing, dosage, and efficacy of exercise-associated RES. Although the results are promising, with several studies reporting reduced muscle damage and improved recovery, inconsistencies in RES administration timing, dosage, and bioavailability require further investigation. Understanding these factors is critical to optimizing the therapeutic potential of RES in both the exercise and clinical settings. Finally, the review summarizes the potential of RES as a safe and effective intervention for EIMD and implications for future research.

title: From bouts to readiness to compete: temporal dynamics of stress, fatigue, recovery and monitoring-informed decisions in combat sports.
abstract: Combat-sport tournaments require decisions before responses to previous efforts have resolved. Detecting a change does not establish that an indicator predicts the next task or improves a decision. This Perspective proposes a task- and time-specific framework linking prior bouts, recovery time and subsequent demands through three evidentiary requirements. Responsiveness concerns reproducible changes beyond measurement error when an indicator represents a response to effort. Predictive validity concerns anticipation of a pre-specified subsequent outcome and added information beyond simpler measures. Decision utility concerns improved outcomes relative to usual practice. Indicators interpreted as current status or stable capacity need not respond to prior effort, but still require adequate measurement properties and prospective evaluation. Evidence from repeated bouts, recovery interventions, mental fatigue, sleep restriction and weight loss suggests that monitoring domains are not interchangeable. The framework retains discordant indicators, evaluates combinations and communicates uncertainty without global clearance labels. Three hypotheses address task and time dependence, maintained performance with increasing effort cost, and indicator-informed decisions. Medical decisions remain independent and take precedence. This is an operational extension of existing principles, not a validated predictive tool.

title: Ask the experts: a practitioner-centred approach to resilience in emergency medical services.
abstract: Background: Resilience in high-stress occupations is commonly framed as a trait, an outcome, or the absence of psychopathology. None of these framings captures what practitioners in emergency medical services actually do, and interventions built on trait-based models have produced weak or inconsistent effects.Objective: This study argues that frontline resilience in emergency medical services is better understood as a domain-specific expert skill, and that work mode - a deliberately entered state, akin to an athlete's game face, in which the demands of the task rather than the emotional force of the scene govern functioning - is its central empirical signature. The aims were to identify factors that intensify traumatic impact, characterise the strategies practitioners use to maintain functioning, and explore systemic and relational barriers that constrain coping.Method: Twenty Queensland Ambulance Service paramedics and dispatchers (tenure 2-38 years) participated in semi-structured interviews, analysed via reflexive thematic analysis.Results: Three intensifiers of traumatic impact (unpredictability, moral weight, personal threat) defined the operational demands against which resilience was enacted. Three coping themes (baseline buffers, work mode, social scaffolding) described the architecture of sustained functioning. Work mode exhibited the defining features of skilled performance: domain specificity, a phased temporal structure (preparation, containment, recovery), and a developmental trajectory from effortful to automatic execution. Two further themes (organisational distrust, the outsider gap) described the systemic and relational conditions that constrain coping.Conclusions: Treating resilience as expertise shifts the field from descriptive stressor-outcome accounts towards assessable, trainable capacities, and exposes the limitations of trait-based self-report measures that cannot distinguish genuine resilience from unsustainable stoicism.

title: Spatial transcriptomics in immune-mediated necrotising myopathy uncovers a specific necrotic signature related to immune-driven fibrosis.
abstract: Immune-mediated necrotising myopathies (IMNM) are characterised by muscle fibre necrosis, complement deposits around non-necrotic fibres, and macrophage infiltrates. Patients experience muscle damage with fibro-fatty replacement, leading to poor strength recovery, but the pathogenesis remains unclear. To investigate IMNM pathogenesis, we applied spatial transcriptomics on myositis muscle biopsies and integrated the results with published single-nucleus transcriptomic data. This combined approach enabled analysis of gene expression with spatial localisation in the muscle. Inflammatory, fibrotic, regenerative, and lipid metabolism-related signatures were identified in IMNM, distinct from other myositis, with specific distribution in necrotic and peri-necrotic regions. A unique subtype of immune-driven fibroblasts expressing SFRP4 was enriched in IMNM necrotic areas. These cells carried a strong proportion of IMNM-enriched pathological signatures, notably a complement-linked 'tumour-like' inflammatory fibroblast signature and a specific interferon response, characterised by the expression of metallothioneins. Peri-necrotic areas were characterised by pathological muscle signatures carrying interferon response and FABP4+ metabolically dysfunctional signatures. In conclusion, IMNM necrotic muscle areas are linked to a specific SFRP4-expressing fibroblast subtype interacting with macrophages, potentially driving the pathological muscle phenotype and contributing to inflammation, fibro-fatty replacement, and strength loss.

title: Psychological Profiles of Elite Cerebral Palsy Football Players: Comparison With Able-Bodied Athletes.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the psychological profiles of elite cerebral palsy (CP) football players associated with athletic performance. While understanding psychological competencies is vital for high-performance para-sports, data on specific adaptive strategies remain scarce. This study compared 16 elite CP football players with 1,460 able-bodied athletes across four competitive levels (Regional-International) using the JISS-Psychological Test for Elite Athletes, which assesses 10 factors across three categories: psychological skills, self-understanding, and athletic commitment. CP players showed moderate-to-large effects in Imagination and Self-Analysis compared with athletes at all competitive levels (Hedges' g = 0.58-0.98, adjusted p < .05). These findings suggest that elite athletes with CP develop superior internal cognitive strategies to compensate for physical and environmental constraints, such as spasticity and motor uncertainty. The results highlight the importance of psychological support focused on internal simulation and self-reflection to enhance competitive excellence in para-sports.

title: Serum-derived exosomal circENC1 inhibits SMC phenotypic switching to stabilize atherosclerotic plaques by interacting with miR-513a-5p and inhibiting MYH9 degradation.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The function of serum-derived exosomes (serum-exos) that suppress smooth muscle cell (SMC) phenotypic switching-related genes in plaque stabilization is unclear. We aimed to determine the functional role of serum-exos, which are pivotal molecular regulators, in plaque stabilization and the underlying mechanism.
METHODS AND RESULTS: RNA sequencing and bioinformatic analyses of human serum-exos were used to identify circENC1, which is involved in SMC phenotypic switching and plaque stabilization. qRT-PCR assays further confirmed that the circENC1 level was substantially lower in the unstable plaque (UP)-exo group than in the stable plaque (SP)-exo group. In mice treated with serum-exos from patients with SPs, the expression of the SMC contractile phenotype indicators ACTA2 and SM22 and the plaque stability increased. In contrast, in the group treated with serum-exos from patients with UPs, CD68 expression and the vulnerability index were increased. Moreover, circENC1 expression was negatively correlated with the plaque vulnerability index in the UP-exo group and the sham group. Mechanistically, bioinformatics, chromatin isolation by RNA purification (ChIRP) and dual-luciferase reporter assays indicated that circENC1 suppressed SMC phenotypic switching by inhibiting the degradation of MYH9 and acting as a miR-513a-5p sponge to release MYOCD.
CONCLUSION: Serum exosomal circENC1 inhibits SMC phenotypic switching to stabilize plaques by binding to miR-513a-5p and inhibiting MYH9 degradation, indicating that this molecule may play an important role in the clinical diagnosis and treatment of atherosclerotic plaques.

title: When Proxies Overshadow Actual Performance: Reaffirming First Principles in Applied Sport Science.
abstract:
PURPOSE: In recent years, sport science has witnessed a growing emphasis on derived mechanical metrics and complex analytical approaches, often accompanied by claims that direct performance measures, such as jump height or sprint time are misleading or less informative than the proxies intended to explain them. This trend has contributed to a progressive shift away from the primary outcomes of athletic testing and toward secondary descriptors, frequently interpreted as superior indicators of performance. Using the vertical jump as a representative example, this commentary revisits fundamental foundations of classical mechanics and applied sport science to clarify the distinction between performance outcomes and mechanistic descriptors. The purpose of this commentary is to reinforce a fundamental principle of performance assessment: when the intended construct is task performance, direct outcomes, such as vertical jump height, horizontal jump distance, and sprint time should remain the primary reference. Mechanistic measures should be selected when they provide reliable and actionable information about how that outcome was achieved or why it changed.
CONCLUSIONS AND PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: Actual performance outcomes, such as jump height, jump distance, and sprint time are the most meaningful, interpretable, and relevant indicators of athletic performance. Mechanistic variables and detailed analytical approaches may provide valuable insights into underlying movement strategies and efficiency, but they should complement, rather than replace, direct performance measures. Following Occam's razor, applied sport science should continue to embrace scientific advances while avoiding the unnecessary promotion of complex, time-consuming, and expensive technologies as indispensable tools for coaches and practitioners, thereby preserving confidence in simple, valid, and accessible measures of athletic performance.

title: Aerobic exercise preconditioning enhances skeletal muscle resistance and recovery after contusion: involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Compared with passive recovery after injury, exercise preconditioning may provide an active strategy for improving the subsequent response of skeletal muscle to injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of aerobic exercise preconditioning (AEP) on skeletal muscle injury (SMI) and post-injury repair, with particular focus on the involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and changes in PGC-1α acetylation.
METHODS: This study initially investigated the effects of continuous aerobic exercise on skeletal muscle in healthy mice. Subsequently, the influence of AEP on injury severity and regenerative repair of the gastrocnemius muscle was examined in mice with SMI. Western blotting was used to determine the expression levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α proteins, immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the acetylation status of PGC-1α, and qRT-PCR was used to analyze the expression of genes associated with mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers and muscle regeneration. Finally, the involvement of SIRT1 signaling in the AEP-associated response to SMI was further examined using the pharmacological SIRT1 inhibitor EX527.
RESULTS: Continuous aerobic exercise was associated with increased SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling and changes in mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers in the gastrocnemius muscle of healthy mice. AEP was associated with reduced injury-related changes and an improved post-injury repair profile in mice with SMI. During the early stage after injury, AEP was accompanied by sustained SIRT1/ PGC-1α signaling and reduced PGC-1α acetylation. Pharmacological inhibition of SIRT1 with EX527 partially attenuated the AEP-associated protective and reparative effects on the injured gastrocnemius muscle.
CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that AEP establishes an adaptive state in skeletal muscle that is associated with reduced injury-related damage and an enhanced post-injury reparative response. The SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and altered PGC-1α acetylation may contribute to these AEP-associated effects.

title: Task Force 8: Care of Competitive Athletes with Arrhythmias and Sudden Cardiac Arrest: Clinical Considerations and Electrocardiogram Interpretations.
abstract: This document outlines recommendations for managing competitive athletes with arrhythmias and risks of sudden cardiac arrest, emphasizing individualized risk assessment, shared decision-making, and return-to-play protocols tailored to each athlete's cardiac profile and sport demands. It provides evaluation strategies for ventricular arrhythmias, implantable cardiac defibrillators, atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia, Wolff-Parkinson-White pattern/syndrome, and syncope, alongside guidance for electrocardiogram interpretation in athletes. A key focus is placed on differentiating between low-risk and high-risk conditions, with recommendations for treatment strategies and ongoing monitoring to ensure athletes' safety.

title: Running the Numbers: High Metabolic Load Distance as an Alternative to Traditional External Load Metrics in Elite Women's Football.
abstract: This study examined the relationship between High Metabolic Load Distance (HMLD) and both session RPE (sRPE) and athlete wellness in women's football and compared it with traditional load monitoring metrics. An observational design was used to collect data from one elite women's football team during training and games in the 2024/25 A-League W season. Twenty-four athletes wore global positioning devices to capture external load metrics, including total distance (TD), high-speed running distance (HSRD) and HMLD. Session RPE and daily wellness were collected through online questionnaires. Generalised additive models were used to examine non-linear relationships between external load, subsequent days' wellness and RPE, and relationships between morning wellness and same-day external load. Higher load was associated with increased sRPE, and poorer next-day wellness, with effects diminishing within two to 3 days post-session. Across all outcomes, HMLD demonstrated stronger and more consistent relationships than TD and HSRD, explaining a greater proportion of variance in wellness and sRPE. Same-day wellness was associated with differences in distances, with higher motivation and lower fatigue corresponding to higher HMLD. HMLD demonstrated comparatively stronger associations with immediate perceived exertion and short-term athlete reported wellness than traditional distance-based metrics in this cohort. These findings support the application of HMLD as a practical and sensitive measure to inform training decision-making in elite women's football.

title: Shoulder Arthritis.
abstract: Glenohumeral osteoarthritis is a common, debilitating joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss, subchondral bone remodeling, and capsular stiffness, leading to pain, restricted motion, and functional impairment. Diagnosis relies on both clinical evaluation and imaging studies. Classification systems, such as the Walch classification, assist in assessing disease severity and guiding treatment decisions. Management begins with conservative approaches, including nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), physical therapy, and intra-articular injections, progressing to surgical interventions such as total or reverse shoulder arthroplasty for advanced disease. Early diagnosis and patient-specific treatment are essential to ensuring optimal patient outcomes.

title: 660 nm LED preconditioning programs mitochondrial signaling in BMSCs for functional tracheal cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Stem-cell-based cartilage regeneration is limited not only by cell delivery, but also by the difficulty of establishing a stable and functionally competent regenerative cell state before implantation. Here, we report a photonic mitochondrial programming strategy in which 660 nm light-emitting diode (LED) irradiation preconditions bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) to enhance functional tracheal cartilage regeneration. BMSCs were seeded onto egg white-derived ring-shaped porous scaffolds and exposed to defined 660 nm LED irradiation before implantation. Among the tested irradiation conditions, 15 J/cm2 optimally promoted BMSC proliferation, chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition, while suppressing fibrotic, hypertrophic and matrix-degrading phenotypes. Mechanistically, 660 nm LED irradiation enhanced cytochrome c oxidase (CCO) activity, mitochondrial membrane potential, adenosine triphosphate (ATP) production and respiratory function, accompanied by moderate reactive oxygen species (ROS) signaling. This mitochondrial bioenergetic-redox response activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR/GSK3β-SOX9 axis, thereby promoting type II collagen, aggrecan and glycosaminoglycan-rich matrix formation. Pharmacological inhibition of ROS signaling, mitochondrial activity, PI3K or mTOR attenuated the LED-induced chondrogenic program. In a rabbit tracheal cartilage ring defect model, 15 J/cm2-preconditioned BMSC-scaffold constructs improved cartilage-like tissue formation, airway epithelial repair, lumen patency and mechanical support after 30 days of observation. These findings support 660 nm LED irradiation as a controllable mitochondrial preconditioning strategy for stem-cell-based functional cartilage regeneration.

title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model.
METHOD: ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring.
RESULTS: In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

title: Creating Consensus: Establishing a Definition of Sports Pharmacy and Its Emerging Role in Sports Medicine.
abstract: Sports pharmacy has become an increasingly recognized specialty within the broader pharmacy profession and serves as a complementary discipline to sport medicine. Yet, the field has lacked a formally established, internationally accepted definition. The absence of standardized terminology has hindered academic integration, interprofessional collaboration, and policy development. This work aimed to establish the first consensus-derived definition of sports pharmacy, accompanied by a responsibility statement to guide future education, certification, and research. In 2024, the US Sports Pharmacy Group (USSPG), comprising pharmacists, academics, anti-doping professionals, student pharmacists, and competitive athletes from diverse US states and international settings, convened a discrete subgroup, the Define Sports Pharmacy Taskforce, to lead the development of a formal definition of sports pharmacy. The taskforce conducted a thematic analysis of existing literature and reviewed 123 open-ended member responses collected between 2022 and 2024. Eight recurring practice themes emerged and informed iterative drafting cycles. Draft definitions were subsequently reviewed by interprofessional stakeholders, including physicians, elite athletes, and anti-doping practitioners. The resulting definition emphasizes medication management, anti-doping advocacy, interprofessional collaboration, athlete-centered ethical care, and the use of therapeutic and pharmacological strategies to optimize performance, support recovery, and protect sports integrity across all levels of physical activity. This consensus-derived framework provides standardized terminology to support the development of educational pathways, establish certification standards, and promote the integration of pharmacists into athlete support teams.

title: Delayed Diagnosis of Achilles Tendon Rupture in a 75-Year-Old Patient with Bimalleolar Ankle Fracture: A Case Report.
abstract:
CASE: A 75-year-old woman sustained a minimally displaced bimalleolar ankle fracture after a fall. An ipsilateral Achilles tendon rupture was missed until day 26, when persistent heel pain and inability to plantarflex prompted an MRI, revealing a rupture with a 5.5-cm gap. Both injuries were treated nonoperatively using controlled ankle motion (CAM) boots, heel wedges, progressive weight bearing, and rehabilitation. At 12 months, the patient had resumed independent ambulation.
CONCLUSION: All ankle fracture patients should undergo systematic Achilles tendon assessment with early follow-up reassessment and a low threshold for advanced imaging when the initial examination is limited.

title: Flexible and stretchable bioelectronics for sports wearable monitoring: Materials, Device Engineering, and Intelligent Wearable Platforms.
abstract: Modern sports science is undergoing a paradigm shift from subjective coaching to objective, data-driven precision training. Consequently, wearable electronics for acquiring precise data during sports activities are attracting attention. However, conventional rigid wearables inherently suffer from mechanical mismatches between rigid wearables and the soft, deformable human skin, inducing severe motion artifacts and restricting natural biomechanics during high-intensity athletic activities. To address these limitations from a comprehensive perspective, this review systematically summarizes and analyzes recent advancements in next-generation flexible and stretchable bioelectronics tailored specifically for sports applications. We systematically examine the substrate materials, structural engineering designs, and device-level optimization strategies required to withstand repetitive strain, shear, and sweat-intensive environments. Building upon these conformable bio-interfaces, we discuss three core sensing modalities: electrochemical sensors for real-time analysis of sweat biomarkers, biophysical sensors for continuous electrophysiological and hemodynamic monitoring, and electromechanical sensors for high-fidelity kinematic and impact tracking. Furthermore, we discuss body-derived energy harvesting strategies to power sports wearables and wireless communication systems for continuous athletic monitoring. The importance of artificial intelligence and machine learning is increasing, as these techniques enable the removal of motion artifacts and facilitate objective analysis of athletic data for training and health monitoring applications. By evaluating targeted applications across aerobic and anaerobic exercise, cognitive state assessment, and post-exercise recovery, this review demonstrates how next-generation sports wearables contribute to the shift in sports science from reactive treatment toward proactive, data-driven performance enhancement and injury prevention.

title: Pre-season friendly match-play as a double-edged sword: Performance gains and inflammatory cost in semi-professional soccer players (a natural experiment).
abstract: Pre-season training prepares soccer players for competition, but the longitudinal effects of friendly match exposure remain unclear. We investigated whether cumulative late pre-season match-play is associated with physiological adaptation in semi-professional players. Twenty-four male players from a randomly selected semi-professional team competing at national level were assessed at pre-season start, mid-pre-season and pre-competition. Measurements included body composition, physical performance, aerobic fitness and blood markers reflecting muscle damage, inflammation, hormonal status and haematological adaptation. Based on cumulative playing time across eight friendly matches, as determined by coaching staff, players were classified retrospectively into extended play (EP) or limited play (LP) groups. Controlling for mid-pre-season baseline, the EP group showed significantly lower pre-competition values for body mass ( η p 2 = 0.276), body fat ( η p 2 = 0.294) and 35 m sprint time ( η p 2 = 0.129) and higher values for lower-limb power (dominant/non-dominant; η p 2 = 0.219-0.424), velocity at maximal oxygen uptake ( η p 2 = 0.441) and at second ventilatory threshold ( η p 2 = 0.708), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase ( η p 2 = 0.296), myoglobin ( η p 2 = 0.199), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ( η p 2 = 0.920), interleukin-6 ( η p 2 = 0.893), tumour necrosis factor-α ( η p 2 = 0.937) and red blood cell count ( η p 2 = 0.190) (all P ≤ 0.038). Across all participants, total match-play time was correlated significantly with reductions in body fat (r = -0.47) and increases in lower-limb power (r = 0.44-0.67), second ventilatory threshold (r = 0.55) and inflammatory markers (r = 0.79-0.86) (all P ≤ 0.033). Greater friendly match-play exposure during pre-season was associated with favourable physiological adaptations and a more pronounced physiological and inflammatory response. These findings support friendly match-play as a meaningful physiological stimulus and highlight the importance of balancing match exposure with recovery during pre-season preparation.

title: Gingival mesenchymal stem cells attenuate high glucose-induced gingival fibroblast damage and ferroptosis by upregulating ALDH2.
abstract: Periodontitis is a multifactorial inflammatory disease that results in the loss of periodontal supporting tissues, which is closely associated with diabetes. Moreover, gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) have been identified as a newer source for periodontal tissue reconstruction/regeneration. It has been reported that aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) could alleviate inflammation and promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells in periodontitis by blocking ferroptosis. However, the role of ALDH2 and GMSCs in periodontitis is poorly defined. Transcriptomic data from the periodontitis GSE10334 dataset were used for WGCNA analysis. Hub genes were identified using key modules from WGCNA and ferroptosis-related genes and type 2 diabetes mellitus-associated genes from GeneCards dataset. A periodontitis cell model in vitro was established by high glucose (HG) treatment in human gingival fibroblasts (HGFs). Gene expression was detected using real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and western blot. Cell viability, proliferation, and migration were detected by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), 5-ethynyl-2'-deoxyuridine (EdU), and Transwell assays. Interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, IL-8, and matrix metalloproteinase (MMP1) were determined using ELISA. Lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS), glutathione (GSH), and Fe2+ levels were measured using commercial kits. The gingival mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) morphology and characteristics were identified. GMSCs were co-cultured with HG-induced HGFs in Transwell system to analyze the effect of ALDH2 in GMSCs on HG-induced HGF damage. Herein, integrated bioinformatics analyses (WGCNA on GSE10334 dataset combined with ferroptosis- and type 2 diabetes mellitus-related genes from GeneCards) were applied to identify ALDH2 as a candidate gene. Then, the role and the therapeutic potential of ALDH2-modified GMSCs were investigated in HG-induced HGF injury in vitro. ALDH2 expression was decreased in HG-treated HGFs (P < 0.05), and its overexpression reversed HG-induced HGF cell proliferation and migration inhibition, and inflammation and ferroptosis promotion (P < 0.05). In co-cultured systems, ALDH2 upregulation in GMSCs relieved HG-treated HGF dysfunction and ferroptosis (P < 0.05). GMSCs could protect HGFs from HG-induced dysfunction, inflammatory response, and ferroptosis through upregulating ALDH2, suggesting a potential protective mechanism that may inform future therapeutic strategies for diabetic periodontitis, pending validation in more physiologically relevant models.

title: Gene amplification during differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells towards chondrocytes.
abstract: For decades, gene amplification was described as an attribute of tumor cells and as a physiological mechanism to increase gene copy numbers for the higher protein demand during the development of amphibians and flies. Notably, gene amplification has since been detected in normal mammalian cells during differentiation. Numerous amplified genes detected in tumor cells overlap with amplified genes detected during stem cell differentiation. Since stem cells have a valuable potency in regenerative therapies and since cartilage regeneration is a highly demanded therapeutic strategy, the current study investigated gene amplification dynamics during the chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). Using quantitative PCR, copy number changes were analyzed for genes previously implicated in differentiation, as well as genes amplified in chondrosarcoma, including CDK4, MDM2, AGAP2, CPT1B, SHANK3, TRIB1 and MYC. Amplifications were transient and stage-specific: CDK4, CPT1B and SHANK3 exhibited the highest copy number increases at day 2, followed by a gradual decline by day 7, whereas AGAP2 and MDM2 increased later in differentiation. Laser microdissection of toluidine blue-stained areas revealed heterogeneity in amplification patterns: CDK4 amplification was prominent in areas lacking or showing moderate proteoglycan deposition; CPT1B amplification occurred in regions with absent, moderate or intense proteoglycan deposition; and SHANK3 amplification was restricted to areas with intense proteoglycan deposition. Notably, regions with the strongest proteoglycan staining exhibited no gene amplification, suggesting that gene amplification is an early, transient event that diminishes as differentiation progresses. These findings highlight gene amplification as a mechanism during chondrogenesis, potentially critical for early differentiation stages and genome stability in mature cells.

title: PTHrP suppresses BMP2-induced osteochondral differentiation and preserves cartilage phenotype in mesenchymal stem cells via inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling.
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) has the potential to drive multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to undergo chondral-osteogenic (including hypertrophic chondrocyte) differentiation. Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) plays an essential role in fetal endochondral ossification, although persistent PTHrP stimulation leads to postnatal bone loss. Here, we investigated the effects of PTHrP on BMP2-induced endochondral ossification through hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation of MSCs. We found that silencing PTHrP expression inhibited BMP2-induced chondrogenic, hypertrophic, and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while overexpression of PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and suppressed BMP2-induced hypertrophic differentiation of MSCs. Using stem cell implantation studies in athymic nude mice, we demonstrated that while MSCs with silenced PTHrP expression exhibited significantly reduced endochondral ossification of subcutaneous cartilage, overexpression of PTHrP promoted the growth of subcutaneous cartilage while significantly delaying ossification, leading to the preservation of cartilage phenotype. Mechanistically, we showed that exogenous PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs by up-regulating Sox9 expression and inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings strongly suggest that PTHrP may play an important role in mediating BMP2-induced chondral-osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling, indicating that PTHrP may be exploited for endochondral cartilage-bone tissue engineering.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Osteoarthritis-Microenvironment-Triggered Phase Alteration of Injectable Conductive Hydrogel for Attenuating Cartilage Degradation.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which contributes substantially to chondrocyte dysfunction, oxidative stress, and cartilage degradation. Although stimuli-responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for OA therapy, conventional hydrogel-based systems exhibit limited sensitivity and require external detection equipment, highlighting the need for a simple, sensitive, and directly observable monitoring system. To address these challenges, we developed a ROS-triggered, in situ-forming gel-sol transition of a polydopamine (PDA)-loaded, diselenide-crosslinked polymer dot (PD) injectable hydrogel (HGC-PDA@PD or OA gel) as a monitorable theranostic for OA therapy at physiological temperature (37°C). The monitorable OA microenvironment-responsive hydrogel relied on interactions between the high ROS levels in OA cartilage and the OA gel, which triggered diselenide bond cleavage and the release of PDA from PD, causing a unique gel-sol transition of the OA gel. Owing to PDA release after diselenide breakage, the fluorescence and electroconductivity of the OA gel changed, which could serve as additional signals during OA detection. In vitro studies demonstrated the sensitive gel-sol transition of OA gel towards OA-induced immature articular chondrocytes (IL-1β/siSOD1/siCatalase-transfected iMACs). Furthermore, the OA gel showed a distinct gel-sol transition in cartilage of an in vivo OA mouse model compared with that in control mice. The lower transcription levels of cartilage matrix-degrading enzymes (ADAMTS4, ADAMTS5, MMP-3, and MMP-13) observed after OA gel injection confirmed that the OA gel could scavenge ROS and attenuate cartilage damage, revealing its potential application for dual-function OA diagnosis and rehabilitation.

title: Ethanol-induced alterations in mesenchymal stromal cells and the effects of aspalathin: implications for alcohol-associated osteonecrosis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alcohol-associated osteonecrosis is a debilitating condition characterized by progressive bone destruction. Although mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) play a critical role in tissue repair, the effects of chronic alcohol exposure on MSCs and their responsiveness to microenvironmental signals remain unclear.
METHODS: MSCs were exposed to ethanol (EtOH) to evaluate changes in viable cell number, ROS-related fluorescence signals, and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. CXCL12 expression was examined in human femoral head specimens and ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. The effects of aspalathin (ASP) on EtOH-induced alterations in MSCs were also investigated.
RESULTS: EtOH exposure reduced viable MSC number and increased ROS-related fluorescence signals. It was also associated with decreased expression of ATP5A and CXCR4 and increased expression of p16. CXCL12 expression was higher in alcohol-associated osteonecrosis tissue than in osteoarthritis tissue and appeared qualitatively increased in ethanol-exposed osteocyte-like cells. These findings indicate altered CXCL12 and CXCR4 expression across the tissue and in vitro experimental settings. ASP treatment attenuated the EtOH-induced reduction in the CCK-8 signal, was associated with attenuation of ROS-related fluorescence signals, significantly restored ATP5A expression, suppressed p16 expression, and showed a non-significant trend toward recovery of CXCR4 expression.
CONCLUSIONS: Ethanol exposure was associated with alterations in the cellular state of MSCs, accompanied by changes in ROS-related fluorescence signals and the expression of mitochondrial-related, senescence-associated, and chemokine signaling-related molecules. ASP partially attenuated some of these ethanol-induced alterations. Further studies are required to clarify the functional significance of these findings and to validate them in vivo.

title: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA)-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in a subset of professional soccer players.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Exercise-related signal abnormality (ERSA) is a relatively new MRI entity described in professional soccer players. We report a subset of players who sustained acute muscle injuries and ERSA lesions in the same muscle.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted from July 2024 to July 2026 to identify all MRI studies of professional soccer players with an acute thigh muscle injury and ERSA lesion in the same muscle. Anatomical site, laterality, ERSA lesion subtype and length, and acute muscle injury grade as per the British Athletics Muscle Injury Classification (BAMIC) were recorded.
RESULTS: There were 18 ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries in 16 soccer players (12 males, 4 females; median age 20.5 years). Affected muscles were the rectus femoris (n = 12), adductor longus (n = 5), and semitendinosus (n = 1). Type C ERSA lesions (n = 13) and BAMIC grade 2b (n = 8) muscle injuries were the most common. All acute muscle injuries were located within the ERSA lesions. No intratendinous extension was observed. Median ERSA lesion length was 21.5 cm and median acute muscle injury length was 7.0 cm. The main ERSA-associated muscle injury patterns were pre-degloving (n = 6) and myofascial (n = 6) injuries of the rectus femoris and distal myotendinous junction injuries of the adductor longus (n = 4).
CONCLUSION: We describe a new muscle injury pattern, termed ERSA-associated acute thigh muscle injuries, in a cohort of professional soccer players. Distinct injury patterns were observed in the rectus femoris and adductor longus.

title: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats is partially mediated by enhancing necroptosis via phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 h of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study links Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1)-sensitive receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL)-associated signaling with biochemical, histological, inflammatory, and functional outcomes after rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury. Nec-1 reduced RIPK1 and MLKL phosphorylation, muscle injury, and early functional impairment. These findings extend prior skeletal-muscle studies by integrating molecular pathway activation with longitudinal functional recovery while supporting a contribution of RIPK1-associated necroptotic signaling.

title: Analytical strategies for distinguishing endogenous and exogenous anabolic androgenic steroids in doping control.
abstract: Doping control for anabolic androgenic steroids (AASs) must separate endogenous physiology from exogenous administration when the same molecular entities occur on both sides of the boundary. This Critical Review evaluates analytical strategies for that source-attribution problem, with emphasis on urinary steroid profiling, longitudinal interpretation, compound-specific isotope ratio mass spectrometry, intact phase-II metabolites, alternative matrices, high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), and data-driven evidence integration. Current practice relies on a staged logic: routine steroid-profile measurements define marker behavior, the steroidal module of the Athlete Biological Passport (ABP) evaluates individual changes, and gas chromatography-combustion-isotope ratio mass spectrometry (GC-C-IRMS) supplies orthogonal source evidence when pseudo-endogenous steroids or atypical profiles require confirmation. UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B17 (UGT2B17) deletion, sex, menstrual-cycle phase, pregnancy, medication, and sample degradation can alter marker concentrations and ratios. Intact conjugates, dried blood spots (DBS), HRMS metabolite discovery, and statistical tools can provide additional evidence, but their performance depends on validation for the relevant matrix and administration scenario. The most defensible strategy is therefore a tiered framework that combines longitudinal interpretation, source-specific chemical evidence, and expert review.

title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR-/- -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
abstract: The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR-/- deficiency-mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone2:5/polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL2:5/PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR-/- mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo-loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR-/- cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo-loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR-/- mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency-related bone diseases.

title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
abstract: The 2025 Orthopaedic Trauma Association's Basic Science Focus Forum featured a symposium on regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies for orthopaedic trauma. Four experts presented complementary perspectives on the next generation of bone and soft tissue repair: Dr. J. Tracy Watson described how orthobiologics and refined spacer design can be used to engineer a better Masquelet induced membrane; Dr. Lauren Priddy presented evidence that hydroxyapatite coatings can mitigate the rapid degradation of additively manufactured magnesium scaffolds; Dr. Vaida Glatt described the development and clinical translation of the Biomimetic Hematoma scaffold for bone and muscle regeneration; and Dr. Katherine Hixon outlined how the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) can serve as a framework to accelerate musculoskeletal regenerative engineering. Collectively, the symposium underscored a shift toward biologically informed, clinically predictive, and ethically responsible engineering solutions for the patients who sustain musculoskeletal trauma.
journal: OTA international : the open access journal of orthopaedic trauma

title: Longitudinal association between vertical jump performance and sprint acceleration performance in sprinters.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed at investigating the associations between changes in sprint performance and changes in vertical jump performances and to clarify whether the vertical jump performances would reflect better sprint acceleration performance.
METHODS: To examine the association between changes in sprint performance and vertical jump performance, two experimental sessions per participant were conducted using an identical protocol with a one- or two-month interval. Seventeen male sprinters performed a 60-m sprint and 3 vertical jump tests in each test session.
RESULTS: The change in 60-m sprint time was correlated with changes in countermovement jump (CMJ) height (r=-0.573) and ankle continuous rebound jump (AJ) contact time (r=0.660). Changes in sprint acceleration were correlated with changes in squat jump (SJ) height from the 10th to 16th steps (r=0.495-0.676), with changes in CMJ height from the 13th to 16th steps (r=0.509-0.587), with changes in AJ height from the 15th to 19th steps (r=0.493-0.583), with changes in AJ contact time from the 8th to 14th steps (r=-0.499 to -0.570), and with changes in AJ index from the 15th to 19th steps (r=0.496-0.627).
CONCLUSIONS: The SJ and CMJ heights, as well as AJ contact time, may likely be indicators of better sprint acceleration performance during the middle acceleration section, while AJ height and index are likely useful for indirectly assessing sprint acceleration performance during the final acceleration section. Sprinters and coaches can use these vertical jumps for monitoring changes in sprint performance for the entire distance and specific acceleration sections.
journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness

title: Stem cell therapy attenuates cerebellar histological alterations and blood-brain barrier disruption in experimental fibromyalgia: involvement of mast cells, autophagy, and NLRP3/IL-1β neuroinflammatory pathway.
abstract: Fibromyalgia is a prevalent and debilitating condition that results in generalized musculoskeletal pain, trouble sleeping, exhaustion, psychological challenges, and social problems. As a consequence of fibromyalgia's substantial therapeutic and socioeconomic burden caused by its high prevalence, uncertain etiology, wide spectrum of clinical manifestations, and sophisticated therapy, a considerable interest has emerged in investigating novel aspects of its pathophysiology, particularly those related to anxiety, depression, and cerebellar histological alterations. Such investigations may contribute to the development of effective therapeutic strategies, including the use of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) as a promising treatment approach. Rats were randomly divided into three groups: control, fibromyalgia and fibromyalgia-stem cell groups. Behavioral assessment was carried out. Cerebellar cortices were collected for histological, immunohistochemical, and morphometric analysis. Fibromyalgia group revealed anxiety-like behavioral changes, and neurodegenerative changes with blood-brain barrier (BBB) affection. Furthermore, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression were significantly increased, with significant increase in the total number of mast cells with marked degranulation. Additionally, there was a significant decrease in Calbindin D-28k (CB), Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. Fibromyalgia-stem cells group revealed amelioration in behavioral alterations, histological improvement, significant decrease in CD117, NLRP3 and IL-1β immune-expression, besides a significant increase in CB, Beclin-1 and LC3 immune-expression. This study represents one of the first experimental studies investigating the potential therapeutic value of BMSCs therapy in fibromyalgia-related cerebellar damage through neuroprotective mechanisms involving enhancement of autophagy, mast cell deactivation, and suppression of NLRP3/IL-1β mediated neuroinflammation with improvement of BBB structural integrity.

title: Speed at the edge of stability: a recovery-limited model of metabolic flux in the cheetah.
abstract: The cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) achieves unmatched terrestrial speed through anatomical and muscular specialization for explosive power. Its type IIX glycolytic muscle phenotype, phosphocreatine (PCr) buffering and rapid glycolysis supply adenosine triphosphate at exceptionally high rates. This design enables acceleration but carries a metabolic cost: PCr is depleted, inorganic phosphate (Pi) and proton balance are disturbed, lactate is redistributed, and glucose and glycogen are used. We propose that feeding ecology may add to this cost. After a successful hunt, a substantial carcass meal imposes a second load through gastric acid secretion, the alkaline tide, pancreatic and biliary bicarbonate flux, bile acid signalling, and amino acid and lipid processing. Recovery starts when the chase ends, but its components resolve at different rates. PCr resynthesis and lactate transport may begin within minutes, whereas acid-base and electrolyte normalization, glycogen replenishment and intermediary-metabolite clearance may take longer. Feeding may therefore begin while slower recovery processes remain active, allowing the two loads to overlap. The model predicts that shorter hunt-to-feed or inter-meal intervals will increase the magnitude, duration or cumulative carry-over of acid-base, electrolyte and metabolomic perturbations. Direct cheetah evidence includes the fast-glycolytic muscle phenotype, high spot urinary creatinine concentrations, abundant urinary organic acids and altered acylcarnitine profiles. The timing and interaction of sprint recovery, digestion and metabolite clearance remain unmeasured. This Perspective integrates the adaptations that permit exceptional speed with their potential metabolic costs and provides a testable framework for evaluating how feeding ecology and managed feeding schedules influence recovery.

title: An equine bone marrow aspirate concentrate protocol yields a predictable cellular and cytokine profile.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) is a quick, minimally invasive, point-of-care therapy for equine orthopaedic injuries. Despite growing clinical use, standardised manufacturing methods are lacking, and the final product remains poorly characterised.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a reproducible protocol for equine BMAC production that yields predictable cellular and cytokine compositions.
STUDY DESIGN: In vitro analytical study.
METHODS: Bone marrow aspirate (BMA) was harvested from the sternum of eight healthy adult horses and filtered to remove possible bony spicules. After centrifugation at 1000 × g for 10 min, the buffy coat was collected to generate BMAC. Cellular composition was assessed using standard haematology and cytology, and cytokine concentrations were measured using commercially available enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits. Data are presented as mean ± standard deviation.
RESULTS: BMA filtration successfully removed potential bony material without significantly altering the cellular profile. Cells were predictably concentrated in BMAC: total nucleated cells increased from 77 ± 30 × 103/μL to 240 ± 57 × 103/μL; and platelets from 119 ± 34 × 103/μL to 269 ± 81 × 103/μL. Anti-inflammatory cytokines were increased in BMAC: IL-1ra increased from 18,611.3 ± 5509.1 to 36,598.8 ± 5971.8 pg/mL; IL-10 from 9.0 ± 7.5 to 19.1 ± 15.6 ng/mL; and TGF-β1 from 2535.0 ± 3018.7 to 5073.8 ± 2175.9 pg/mL. Of the pro-inflammatory cytokines measured, only IL-1β was increased (287.5 ± 22.5 to 475.1 ± 206.0 pg/mL), while TNF-α and IL-6 were unchanged.
MAIN LIMITATIONS: The small cohort size (n = 8) limited sensitivity for detecting minor effects. The cytokine panel, while representative, does not encompass all potential bioactive mediators, and single-time-point measurements do not necessarily reflect in vivo release kinetics. The clinical efficacy of BMAC was not evaluated, preventing direct correlation between compositional features and therapeutic outcomes.
CONCLUSIONS: The BMAC protocol yielded consistently concentrated nucleated cells, preserved cellular morphology, and enhanced the anti-inflammatory cytokine profile relative to post-filtration BMA. These findings provide a biological rationale for intra-articular and intra-lesional use of BMAC in equine patients.

title: Adhesive hydrogel-mediated spatiotemporal delivery of garlic-derived nanovesicles reprograms immunometabolism to rescue periodontal bone regeneration.
abstract: The core challenge in regenerating inflammatory bone defects, such as periodontitis-related bone resorption, lies in the dysregulation of the immune-metabolic microenvironment, which required implanted materials to simultaneously possess tissue sealing properties, sustained immune modulation capacity and metabolic intervention functions. Herein, garlic-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (GaELNs), exhibiting anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities, are embedded in an injectable, tissue-adhesive polyethylene glycol hydrogel (GaE-PEG) to meet the challenges. The hydrogel exhibited favorable tissue adhesion and sustained release of GaELN-associated protein in vitro. GaE-PEG promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In lipopolysaccharide-stimulated periodontal ligament stem cells, GaE-PEG alleviated mitochondrial oxidative stress, restored oxidative phosphorylation, suppressed excessive glycolysis, and enhanced osteogenic differentiation. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses linked these effects to mitochondrial metabolic regulation, while oligomycin treatment attenuated the osteogenic response, supporting a contribution of oxidative phosphorylation. In a rat model of periodontitis-related bone defects, GaE-PEG reduced local inflammation and promoted alveolar bone regeneration, with improved regenerative outcomes compared with a single local injection of free GaELNs at an equivalent dose and Bio-Gide™/Bio-Oss™ treatment. These findings support an adhesive hydrogel strategy integrating local nanovesicle delivery with immunomodulation and metabolic regulation to promote bone regeneration under inflammatory conditions.

title: Effects of Intramuscular Mesenchymal Stem Cell and Boric Acid Administration on Muscle Damage and Recovery in an Exhaustive Swimming Rat Model.
abstract: Exhaustive exercise induces damage to skeletal muscle, reducing athletic performance and delaying recovery. Effective experimental strategies are needed to mitigate this damage and accelerate tissue regeneration. This study aimed to address limitations in the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-like cells (MSCs) associated with limited cell viability by evaluating boric acid (BA) as an antioxidant and metabolic modulator to enhance cell viability and muscle repair. Twenty-five female Wistar albino rats underwent a 15 day exhaustive swimming protocol and received intramuscular injections of MSCs (1 × 106 cells), BA (10 µg), or their combination, according to the experimental group allocation. Bone marrow obtained from five additional donor rats was used exclusively for MSC isolation and culture. Daily exhaustion time, serum biomarkers lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase (CK), and gastrocnemius histology were evaluated. Intramuscular BA improved endurance and reduced biochemical markers of muscle injury, whereas MSC application promoted structural muscle regeneration, as evidenced by centrally located nuclei and improved muscle fiber integrity. Combined MSCs + BA treatment improved several biochemical and histological outcomes compared with exercise alone. Serum lactate concentrations remained elevated in treated groups 24 h after the final exercise session, indicating altered post-exercise metabolic responses. Overall, intramuscular BA modulated metabolic responses, whereas administration of bone marrow-derived stromal/stem cell-like cells was associated with structural regeneration in this rat model of exercise-induced skeletal muscle injury, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating regenerative interventions.
